note: Files outside libs/plugins/** that carry a plugin's domain today (AGL-3080): a domain-named file or route directory, a vendor literal, a quoted first-party plugin id, a static plugin import, a plugin-owned Firestore collection addressed from outside the plugin, exports that are mostly one plugin's vocabulary, or ANY declaration in a plugin's vocabulary mixed into a platform file. The last three were added by the content sweep of 2026-09-20, which is the one time this list grew: the rules were new, the files were not. `lane` is the line of AGL-3080's move set that takes the file out; `"lane": "stays"` is a binding argued to be the platform's own, with the argument in `why`. Read by check-plugin-domain-in-core.mjs, which is red for a finding missing here AND for a row or rule nothing trips any more (`--prune` drops those). This list may shrink and must never grow: a new finding is refused, not recorded.

files.why: `'inbox'` here is the notification tray's own tab, beside `'archive'` — a user's unread notifications. It is not the Inbox plugin and reads nothing of it.
Legal text names the vendors it discloses.
The subprocessor inventory discloses every vendor by name; naming them is its whole job, and a plugin-declared row still folds in through the subprocessor seam.
Aglyn's own signup funnel, not a tenant feature.
Aglyn's own console and docs surfaces, not a tenant feature: the operator's tags, swapped with the operator identity on a self-host.
One postal-address shape (AGL-1133); generic despite the name, and no CRM vocabulary is in it.
The designer's generic form controls; nothing of the forms plugin's model.
Generic field definitions for any data-driven form; nothing of the forms plugin.

`'marketing'` here is a SEND PURPOSE, the legal category opposite `'transactional'` that decides which identity and which consent rules apply to a message. Any sender has it, whether or not the Marketing plugin exists.
